job.title: Cable Spooling Technician
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.


We are looking for a Cable Spooling Technician located in Odessa, TX. This is your opportunity to join a global technology company, driving energy innovation for a balanced planet.

 

What’s In It For You:  

  • You will join a growing company offering competitive pay and benefits 
  • Access to best-in-class resources, tools, and technology 
  • Opportunity for a long term, advanced career path 
  • A culture that values safety first, including training and personal protection 

 

What You Will Do: 

  • Drive spooling truck and pull spooling trailer to customer rig site 
  • Perform customer support activities for electrical submersible pumps 
  • Inspect and repair cable 
  • Using pneumatic and manual hand tools, bands cable as it is being installed into the well hole 
  • Complete DOT paperwork as required 
  • Adjust quickly to changing job assignments/requirements and the flexibility to work overtime with little or no advance notice 
  • Maintain truck and trailer per Company standards 

 

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Must have a valid Class A CDL and an acceptable driving record 
  • 1 year experience splicing electrical cable, spooling cable, and CT line 
  • Demonstrated ability to perform and repair armor on cable 
  • Demonstrated ability to band cable or CT line with a Forum banding tool 
  • Excellent customer service skills including the ability to explain and train 
  • Ability to interact politely and professionally with customers and/or coworkers 
  • Immigration sponsorship not offered for this role 
  • Work in excess of 8 hours per day and 40 hours per week, as required to meet business needs 

  

Physical Demands:

  • Role is deemed safety-sensitive and may be subject to employer or customer drug testing. 
  • The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.  Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. 
  • Exerting up to 50 pounds of force occasionally and/or up to 20 pounds of force frequently, and/or up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects. 
  • Ascending or descending ladders, stairs, scaffolding, ramps, poles, and the like, using feet and legs and/or hands and arms. Body agility is emphasized. 
  • Maintaining body equilibrium to prevent falling when walking, standing, or crouching on narrow, slippery, or erratically moving surfaces. 
  • Bending body downward and forward by bending spine at the waist. This factor is important if it occurs to a considerable degree and requires full use of the lower extremities and back muscles. 
  • Bending legs at knee to come to a rest on knees. 
  • Bending the body downward and forward by bending leg and spine. 
  • Moving about on hands and knees or hands and feet. 
  • Extending hand(s) and arm(s) in any direction. 
  • Moving about on foot to accomplish tasks, particularly for long distances or moving from one work site to another. 
  • Using upper extremities to press against something with steady force in order to thrust forward, downward, or outward. 
  • Using upper extremities to exert force in order to draw, drag, haul, or tug objects in a sustained motion. 
  • Raising objects from a lower to a higher position or moving objects horizontally from position to position. 
  • Picking, pinching, typing, or otherwise working, primarily with fingers rather than the whole hand or arm as in handling. 
  • Applying pressure to an object with the fingers and palm. 
  • Perceiving attributes of objects, such as size, shape, temperature, or texture by touching with skin, particularly that of fingertips. 
  • Expressing or exchanging ideas by means of the spoken word.  Those activities in which they must convey detailed or important spoken instructions to customer or other workers accurately, loudly, or quickly. 
  • Perceiving the nature of sounds at normal speaking levels with or without correction.  Ability to receive detailed information through oral communication, and to make the discriminations in sound. 
  • Substantial movement (motions) of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers to use a computer. 
  • The employee is required to have close visual acuity to perform an activity such as: visual inspection involving small defects, small parts and/or operation of machines (including inspection), using measurement devices, and/or assembly or fabrication of parts at distances close to the eyes. 
  • The employee is required to have visual acuity to operate motor vehicles. 
  • The employee is required to have visual acuity to determine the accuracy, neatness, thoroughness of work assigned or to make general observations of facilities or structures. 
  • Indoor and outdoor environmental conditions.  Activities occur indoors and outdoors. 
  • Extreme heat.  Temperatures above 100 degrees for periods of more than one hour.  Consideration should be given to the effect of other environmental conditions, such as wind and humidity. 
  • Hazards.  Includes a variety of physical conditions, such as proximity to moving mechanical parts, moving vehicles, electrical current or exposure to chemicals. 
  • Atmospheric conditions.  One or more of the following conditions that affect the respiratory system or the skin:  fumes, odors, dust, mists, gases, or poor ventilation. 
  • Oils. There is air and/or skin exposure to oils and other cutting fluids.

job.title: Undergraduate Engineering Co-Op – Scott, LA
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

 

We are looking for a motivated and enthusiastic undergraduate student to join our Undergraduate Engineering Co-Op Program in Scott, Louisiana. This is your opportunity to join a global technology company, driving energy innovation for a balanced planet.

As an Engineering Co-Op, you will gain valuable hands-on experience supporting engineering, manufacturing, plant operations, and continuous improvement initiatives within our Chemical Technologies division.

If you are eager to apply your classroom knowledge to real-world engineering and manufacturing challenges, we invite you to apply. You will collaborate with experienced professionals, contribute to meaningful projects, and develop technical and professional skills that will prepare you for a successful engineering career.


This position is based at our Scott, LA facility, where you will gain practical experience in an industrial manufacturing environment while supporting day-to-day plant operations and engineering projects.


What's in It for You:

  • Hands-On Experience: Apply your academic knowledge to practical engineering, manufacturing, and operational challenges in a plant environment.
  • Professional Development: Gain exposure to engineering processes, manufacturing operations, project management, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Meaningful Projects: Participate in projects that support operational efficiency, equipment performance, safety, quality, and reliability.
  • Collaboration and Mentorship: Work alongside experienced engineers, plant leadership, technical professionals, and cross-functional teams while developing valuable industry connections.
  • Career Development: Strengthen your technical, analytical, problem-solving, communication, and leadership skills in a professional manufacturing environment.
  • Benefits: This position is benefits-eligible in accordance with applicable company policies and program guidelines.

What You Will Do:

As an Engineering Co-Op at our Scott, LA facility, your responsibilities may include:

  • Support plant engineering and manufacturing initiatives that contribute to operational efficiency, productivity, safety, and quality.
  • Assist with planning, coordinating, executing, and monitoring engineering projects and plant operational activities.
  • Collaborate with engineering, production, maintenance, quality, and other cross-functional teams to identify opportunities for process improvements.
  • Analyze manufacturing and operational data, identify trends, and recommend opportunities to improve equipment performance and operational efficiency.
  • Participate in technical evaluations, troubleshooting activities, and engineering assessments to support plant operations.
  • Assist with equipment reliability, preventive maintenance, and operational improvement initiatives, as applicable.
  • Support continuous improvement projects focused on productivity, cost efficiency, quality, and process optimization.
  • Assist with preparing engineering documentation, technical reports, project updates, and performance tracking.
  • Gain exposure to manufacturing processes, equipment operations, engineering best practices, and project management principles.
  • Contribute ideas and innovative solutions to improve manufacturing processes, operational effectiveness, and sustainability.
  • Participate in team meetings, project reviews, safety discussions, and professional development opportunities.
  • Demonstrate a commitment to company safety standards, policies, and ethical business practices.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Currently pursuing a bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering or Mechanical Engineering from an accredited college or university.
  • Must have an anticipated graduation date of Spring or Fall 2027.
  • Must be authorized to work in the United States without current or future employer immigration sponsorship.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills.
  • Interest in engineering, manufacturing operations, equipment reliability, or continuous improvement.
  • Previous internship, Co-Op, academic project, or other relevant technical experience.
  • Exposure to manufacturing, industrial, chemical processing, or engineering environments.
  • Basic understanding of engineering principles, manufacturing processes, and project management.
  • Interest in learning about plant operations, equipment performance, and process optimization.
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, and teamwork skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a professional environment.
  • Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.
  • Ability to analyze data, prepare reports, and communicate technical information effectively.
  • Demonstrated willingness to learn, adapt, and take initiative.
  • Strong commitment to workplace safety, quality, and operational excellence.

Additional Information:

This Engineering Co-Op opportunity is based exclusively at our Scott, Louisiana facility and provides hands-on experience in a manufacturing and plant operations environment.

The selected student will have the opportunity to work alongside experienced engineering and operations professionals while contributing to projects that support plant performance, operational efficiency, safety, and continuous improvement.

Specific projects, assignments, and responsibilities will be determined based on facility needs, business priorities, and the student's educational background.

SLB/ChampionX is seeking a Billing support Specialist to provide general administrative support to multiple cross functional departments in Williston, ND/ Dickinson, ND. ·         Opportunity for a long term, advanced career path in finance, supply chain, service, sales, or management

·         Thrive in a company that values a culture of safety to include top-notch safety training and personal protection equipment

job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

 

We are looking for has an immediate opportunity for a Principal Chemist in our Production Chemical Technologies – Flow Assurance and Analytical Services Technology group, located in Calgary, AB.
 

The Technology division is focused on developing innovative and complete solutions to meet our customers’ needs while looking toward the future through our commitment to developing products that satisfy both business and customer needs. Technology is a great place for technical experts to be challenged and make an impact. If you are a passionate professional that likes to work in an autonomous, hands-on environment, we invite you to apply.

Job Overview: 

 

Primarily responsible for testing hydrocarbon samples by GC-FID, GC-MS, Pyrolysis GC-MS, and DSC.  In addition, support the development of new laboratory methods, maintain and troubleshoot lab instrumentation, and provide customer-facing technical support. The applicant should be able to apply subject matter expertise to all aspects of laboratory techniques and testing methodologies.  This position requires a versatile, self-motivated team player with strong interpersonal and organizational skills. 

 

What’s in it For You:

  • Flexible, independent work environment where you will manage a monthly schedule
  • Access to best-in-class resources, tools, and technology
  • Thrive in a company that values a culture of safety, to include top-notch safety training and personal protection equipment
  • Comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, a company-paid pension plan, stock purchase plan, tuition reimbursement and more!
  • Comprehensive benefits package starting day 1 of employment – medical, dental, vision, matching Pension Plan, and more!

 

What Will You Do:

  • Demonstrate safety leadership while actively contributing to a culture of continuous improvement.
  • Provide lab support, analytical data, and interpretation of results for technical and non-technical staff.
  • Work as part of a team to meet a demanding workload while maintaining high standards of accuracy.
  • Collaborate with other team members on projects, experiments, and data analysis.

Position Details:

  • The candidate must reside in Calgary, AB or surrounding areas.
  • Immigration sponsorship is not available for this role.
  • This is a safety-sensitive position, and the successful candidate will be required to complete drug and alcohol testing.
  • This is an on-site role, Monday to Friday.
  • This is a full time role based on 40 hours per week and requires working in a laboratory setting, PPE is required at all times in the lab.

 

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Education and experience should be at a minimum:
    • Bachelor’s degree in a Chemical discipline + 6 years of relevant industry experience, OR
    • Master’s degree + 4 years of relevant industry experience, OR
    • Ph.D. and 2 years of relevant industry experience.
  • In-depth knowledge/experience in gas chromatography, including method development, troubleshooting and maintenance.
  • Proven track record of project management; excellent organizational, time management, and communication skills.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in oilfield production chemicals with a background in Flow Assurance would be an asset.

Physical Demand:

  • Working in a lab environment on regular basis.

job.description:

We are looking for an Account Manager located in Macaé/ RJ - Brazil. This is your opportunity to join a global technology company, driving energy innovation for a balanced planet.


Main Objectives


Plan, lead, and oversee the commercial activities of the account(s) under your responsibility, ensuring the achievement of growth, profitability, market share, and customer satisfaction objectives. Develop sustainable commercial strategies, strengthen relationships with strategic customers, and lead teams in identifying and capturing new business opportunities, in compliance with company policies and guidelines.


Key Responsibilities


  • Develop, implement, and periodically update strategic account and territory management plans.
  • Prepare the annual sales plan, defining goals, strategies, and performance indicators, monitoring execution, and implementing corrective actions when necessary.
  • Lead and develop teams, fostering high performance, engagement, and professional growth.
  • Conduct coaching, performance management, and continuous development of team members.
  • Ensure the execution of the company’s commercial strategy with strategic customers and key accounts.
  • Develop and implement strategies to drive revenue growth, profitability, and market share expansion.
  • Coordinate the introduction of new products, technologies, and solutions to customers.

Requirements

 

  • Bachelor’s degree in chemical engineering, Petroleum Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Chemistry, or a related field.

  • Proven experience in team leadership and development.

Competences


  • Strong results orientation and business growth focus.

  • Ability to negotiate and influence at different organizational levels.
  • Strategic thinking and market analysis capability.
  • Key Account Management expertise.
  • Executive communication and presentation skills.

The support of an organization that believes it is vital to include and engage diverse people, perspectives, and ideas to achieve our best

What You Will Do:

·         Install, commission, configure, test, maintain, and troubleshoot variable speed drives, motor control equipment, SMARTEN controllers, VSD’s and RTUs, legacy Sensia VSD’s, control systems, industrial communications equipment, instrumentation, sensors, SCADA interface equipment, and artificial lift control systems.

·         Perform startup and commissioning activities on new and existing installations.

·         Diagnose and repair electrical, automation, instrumentation, and communication faults in the field.

·         Complete preventive and corrective maintenance on customer equipment.

·         Configure drive parameters, motor control settings, protection functions, communications, and associated control interfaces.

·         Troubleshoot power quality concerns, drive and motor protection alarms, communication failures, instrumentation faults, and controller issues.

·         Verify proper operation of electrical protection, safety circuits, interlocks, instrumentation, and control logic.

·         Assist with product testing, field trials, troubleshooting escalation, and evaluation of new automation technologies.

·         Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives for automation, electrification, artificial lift, and field service products.

·         Shipping and receiving duties

·         Perform bench testing, assembly, inspection, repair, and functional validation of VSDs, controllers, sensors, panels, and related equipment.

·         Prepare systems for shipment, including functional testing, documentation review, packaging, and factory acceptance testing where required.


Pre-Employment Requirements:

  • Drug and alcohol testing
  • Fitness-to-work testing
  • Drivers’ abstract

Position Details:

  • Working at the Lloydminster facility dominantly
  • Working on customer sites or remote locations occasionally
  • Permanent
  • Full-time
  • Mainly working day shift operations, with overtime, or on-call support as required
  • Weekend or night shift may be required dependent on business conditions

·         Travel throughout Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Western Canada as operational requirements dictate.


Required Qualifications:

·        Red Seal Journeyperson Electrician Certificate.

·        Valid Class 5 driver’s license with an acceptable driving record.

·        Industrial electrical experience, including motor controls and VFD/VSD equipment.

·        Ability to safely troubleshoot electrical and electronic control equipment in field and shop environments.

·        Ability to read and interpret electrical drawings, single-line diagrams, control schematics, P&IDs, wiring diagrams, and technical manuals.

·        Working knowledge of AC and DC electrical systems, motor control, industrial instrumentation, and electrical safety practices.

·        Ability to work independently, manage priorities, travel, document work, and communicate professionally with customers and internal teams.


Minimum Qualifications:

·        Oil and gas, artificial lift, production automation, or field-service experience.

·        Experience with legacy Sensia VSD systems, SMARTEN controllers and VSD systems, SCADA systems, RTUs, PLCs, sensors, industrial Ethernet, cellular, radio, or other field communications.

·        Knowledge of production optimization technologies and rod-lift automation.

·        Experience with shop testing, factory acceptance testing, inventory control, shipping, and receiving.

job.title: Ingeniero de procesos
job.description:
ChampionX forma ahora parte de SLB, una empresa tecnológica global que impulsa la innovación energética para un planeta equilibrado. Como innovadores, esa ha sido nuestra misión durante casi un siglo.
Somos una empresa tecnológica que desbloquea el acceso a la energía para el beneficio de todos. Como innovadores, esa ha sido nuestra misión durante casi un siglo. Hoy, nos enfrentamos a un imperativo global de crear un futuro con más energía, pero menos carbono. Nuestros diversos e innovadores agentes de cambio están centrados en avanzar más allá en la innovación e inventar las nuevas tecnologías energéticas que necesitamos para llegar ahí.
Para más noticias e información, visita SLB.com
Síguenos en Facebook en @WeAreSLBGlobal, LinkedIn: SLBGlobal, o Instagram en @SLBGlobal.



¿Qué ganas tú con esto?

 Oportunidad para una trayectoria profesional avanzada y a largo plazo en servicio, ventas o gestión Acceso a recursos, herramientas y tecnología de primera categoría Prosperar en una empresa que valora una cultura de seguridad que incluya formación de primera calidad y equipos de protección personal La oportunidad de impulsar cambios significativos y moldear tu carrera dentro de una empresa dinámica y orientada al crecimiento. Apoyo de una organización comprometida con fomentar la diversidad, la inclusión y la participación para lograr el éxito colectivo. Acceso a Grupos de Recursos para Empleados (ERGs), facilitando la colaboración y fomentando un entorno laboral diverso e inclusivo. Utilización de múltiples plataformas de intercambio de conocimientos para mejorar la colaboración y el compromiso entre equipos. Disfruta de la formación remunerada que te permite aprender de profesionales exitosos Paquete integral de beneficios desde el primer día de empleo.

 

Lo que harás:

•     Cumplir con las políticas de seguridad para garantizar un entorno laboral seguro, alineado con los principios de “Goal Zero” para mejorar continuamente el desempeño en seguridad, salud, medio ambiente, y manejo de productos químicos.

•     Apoyar y comprometerse con el proceso de mejora continua de calidad, promoviendo el trabajo sin errores desde el primer intento.

•     Identificar oportunidades de mejora en los procesos y funciones.

•     Gestionar eficazmente todas las funciones de la cadena de suministro local y desarrollar alianzas colaborativas con colegas y partes externas.

•     Cumplir con los resultados acordados, manteniendo relaciones laborales positivas.



Responsabilidades principales:

   Gestionar proyectos de relocation hacia Plantas ChampionX, garantizando el mejor TDC. 

  Introducción de nuevos productos a Planta Soledad y Planta Quito (seteos en SAP: nueva planta, nuevo empaque). 

  Calcular, hacer seguimiento y garantizar el cumplimiento de los ahorros planeados por proyectos de Relocation.  

  Analizar, validar y reportar en plataformas corporativas los proyectos de ahorro de la región.(CinCO & ChIIP). 

  Crear reportes, analizar y presentar indicadores de gestión de la región (OGSM). 

  Brindar soporte a gerentes de la región en el planteamiento y ejecución de la Planeación Estratégica. 

  Brindar soporte a la dirección con cualquier tipo de asignación de análisis de datos.  

  Coordinar reuniones para definir estrategias y planes para la implementación del proceso de mejora continua en LA en coordinación con lider de mejora continua de la región. 

Requisitos mínimos:

Profesional en ingeniería química o carreras afines. 

Mínimo dos (2) años de experiencia en cargos similares 

 

FORMACIÓN 

 

Dominio avanzado del idioma Inglés 

Manejo avanzado de herramientas ofimáticas (MS Excel, Word, power point) 

Conocimientos básicos en PowerBI 

SQL Server  (deseable)

Requisitos deseables:

Experiencia en entornos de manufactura química.

 

Exigencias físicas:

El puesto se considera sensible a la seguridad y puede estar sujeto a pruebas de drogas del empleador o del cliente.



Acerca de ChampionX:

ChampionX es un líder mundial en la provisión de programas y servicios de química, tecnología de perforación, soluciones de elevación artificial y tecnologías de automatización para la industria del petróleo y gas aguas arriba y Midstream. Nuestra cultura de seguridad de primer nivel alimenta nuestro propósito de mejorar vidas a través de nuestro compromiso con la realización de operaciones sostenibles.



Nuestro compromiso con la diversidad y la inclusión
Creemos que los mejores equipos son diversos e inclusivos, y estamos en un camino para crear un lugar de trabajo donde cada empleado pueda crecer y alcanzar lo mejor de sí mismo. Estamos comprometidos con un trato justo e igualitario para empleados y candidatos. Reclutamos, contratamos, promocionamos, transferimos y ofrecemos oportunidades de ascenso basadas en las cualificaciones individuales y el desempeño laboral. En todos los asuntos que afecten al empleo, la compensación, los beneficios, las condiciones laborales y las oportunidades de ascenso, no discriminaremos a ningún empleado o solicitante de empleo por motivos de raza, religión, color, credo, origen nacional, estatus de ciudadanía, sexo, orientación sexual, identidad y expresión de género, información genética, estado civil, edad, discapacidad o condición de veterano cubierto.
Además, estamos comprometidos a promover los principios de Igualdad de Oportunidades en el Empleo (EEO) a través de la Acción Afirmativa (AA). Nuestro objetivo es aprovechar plenamente a personas de minorías, mujeres, discapacitados y veteranos cubiertos en todos los niveles de la fuerza laboral.

Nuestro compromiso con la diversidad e inclusión 

En ChampionX, creemos que los mejores equipos son diversos e inclusivos, y estamos tratando de crear un lugar de trabajo donde cada socio pueda crecer y lograr lo mejor de sí. Estamos comprometidos con el trato justo y equitativo de los asociados y los postulantes. Reclutamos, contratamos, promovemos, transferimos y brindamos oportunidades para mejorar en función de las calificaciones individuales y el rendimiento laboral. En todas las cuestiones que afectan el empleo, la compensación, los beneficios, las condiciones laborales y las oportunidades para progresar, no discriminaremos a ningún asociado o postulante para el empleo por su raza, religión, color, credo, nacionalidad, estado de ciudadanía, sexo, orientación sexual, identidad de género y sus expresiones, información genética, estado civil, edad, incapacidad o estado como veterano cubierto. 

Además, nos comprometemos a fomentar los principios de Igualdad de oportunidades en el empleo (EEO por sus siglas en inglés) a través de una Acción afirmativa (AA por sus siglas en inglés). Nuestro objetivo es ofrecer empleo plenamente a minorías, mujeres, discapacitados o veteranos cubiertos en todos los niveles de la fuerza laboral.  

Consideraremos para el empleo a todos los postulantes calificados, incluidos aquellos con antecedentes penales, de acuerdo con los requisitos de las leyes estatales y locales pertinentes, incluidas la "Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance" de Los Ángeles y la Fair Chance Ordinance de San Francisco. 

 

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion 

We believe the best teams are diverse and inclusive, and we are on a journey to create a workplace where every employee can grow and achieve their best. We are committed to fair and equal treatment of employees and applicants. We recruit, hire, promote, transfer and provide opportunities for advancement on the basis of individual qualifications and job performance. In all matters affecting employment, compensation, benefits, working conditions, and opportunities for advancement, we will not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, religion, color, creed, national origin, citizenship status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and expressions, genetic information, marital status, age, disability, or status as a covered veteran.

job.title: Guide Operator
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.


We are looking for a Guide Operator located in Pleasanton, TX. This is your opportunity to join a global technology company, driving energy innovation for a balanced planet.


What’s in it For You:

  • The support of an organization that believes it is vital to include and engage diverse people, perspectives, and ideas to achieve our best
  • Thrive in a company that values sustainability, drives a safety-focused culture, and empowers through continuous improvement

What You Will Do:

  • Responsible for the safe and efficient operations of various general machinery, excluding CNC.
  • This includes straighteners, hones, paint equipment, grinders, plating machinery, coating machinery, saws, ovens, and heat-treating equipment.
  • Maintains the highest standards of safety, quality, housekeeping, and environmental awareness at all times.
  • Responsible for the proper documentation and communication of important information to a more senior operator and leadership.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or equivalent and 1-3 years of relevant experience operating similar machinery.
  • Must understand basic math, measurements, and have basic computer skills.
  • Some experience with an ERP system is necessary. Ability to read and understand schematics, drawings, product specifications, and the operation and maintenance of assigned machinery is essential.

Physical Demands:  

  • Must be able to lift and carry 50 lbs regularly.
  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.
  • The employee is regularly required to talk or hear.
  • The employee is frequently required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel and reach with hands and arms.
  • Employee is required to occasionally walk in customer field locations which may include inclines, uneven surfaces, and a variety of weather conditions.
  • Employee must be able to regularly bend, stoop, crawl, lay down, twist and push.
  • Employee is required to wear appropriate personal protective equipment including but not limited to shoes/boots, hard hats, or respirators.
  • Role is deemed safety-sensitive and may be subject to employer or customer drug testing.

  • Perform preventative maintenance as required

·         Working at the Edmonton manufacturing facility

·         Permanent

·         Full-time

·         Rotating shift between day, afternoon and night

Minimum Qualifications:

·         3 years’ experience in a CNC Operator role required

·         Mathematical aptitude required (equations, trigonometry, geometry)

·         Must be able to read blueprints and drawings

·         Must be able to read and understand basic programming

·         Working knowledge of G & M codes required

·         Organized, flexible and able to multi-task

·         Strong verbal communicational skills

·         Reliable

·         High attention to detail


Preferred Qualifications

·         CNC Basic certificate and/or CNC turning center certificate preferred

·         Familiarity of API threads an asset


Physical Demands

·         Ability to lift, push, pull up to 50 lbs.

·         Must be able to stand for a minimum of 8 hours/day

·         Repetitive work

job.title: Sensor Operations Analyst
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.


We are looking for a Sensor Operations Analyst located in Sugar Land, TX. This is your opportunity to join a global technology company, driving energy innovation for a balanced planet


What’s In It For You:

  • Flexible, independent work environment where you will manage a monthly schedule
  • Access to best-in-class resources, tools, and technology
  • Grow your income as you drive growth
  • Thrive in a company that values a culture of safety to include top-notch safety training and personal protection equipment
  • Comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company matching and more

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Science, Engineering, Information Technology, Data Analytics, or a related technical discipline.
  • Minimum 2 years of relevant technical, product support, operations, or data analysis experience.
  • Experience troubleshooting technical systems, devices, software applications, or connectivity issues.
  • Experience working with customers, field personnel, or cross-functional operational teams.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify root causes and drive issue resolution.
  • Experience supporting technical products, connected devices, sensors, or digital solutions.
  • Ability to interpret data, monitor performance metrics, and make operational recommendations.
  • Experience troubleshooting device, software, connectivity, and API-related issues.
  • Proficiency with LLMs, AI, and Automation Tools
  • Demonstrated coding knowledge with experience in Python, SQL, and JavaScript
  • Strong customer service and stakeholder management skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, demand-driven environment.
  • Experience creating and maintaining standard operating procedures (SOPs) and delivering user training.
  • Ability to work independently under general supervision and follow established processes and guidelines.
  • Commitment to safety and adherence to company safety procedures.

What You Will Do:

  • Develop and maintain automation tools and workflow solutions using Python, APIs, LLMs, and data platforms to streamline processes, improve data accuracy, reduce manual effort, and enhance operational efficiency.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for field personnel, customers, and internal stakeholders regarding sensor-related questions, issues, and technical support.
  • Provide troubleshooting, user coaching, and issue resolution for sensor devices, software platforms, connectivity challenges, data transmission, and API integrations.
  • Support device commissioning, configuration, deployment, and ongoing maintenance while ensuring data quality and reliability across a fleet of 12,000+ monitoring devices.
  • Monitor device health, pump variance, dosage accuracy, and key performance indicators through exception-based reporting and proactive performance analysis.
  • Develop and maintain Power BI dashboards, performance tracking tools, and reporting solutions to improve operational visibility and decision-making.
  • Create and enhance Python-based automation tools, workflow improvements, API integrations, and data management solutions to increase efficiency, scalability, and program performance.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 3+ of experience combining technical, digital, and operational responsibilities.
  • Experience supporting IoT, remote monitoring, industrial automation, or sensor-based technologies.
  • Python scripting and process automation experience.
  • Experience working with APIs, databases, and system integrations.
  • Knowledge of chemical injection monitoring, production optimization, or oil and gas operations.
  • Experience with device commissioning, configuration, and deployment activities.
  • Experience managing large device fleets and monitoring device health metrics.
  • Training, onboarding, and change management experience.
  • Experience coordinating with vendors, customers, and field service teams.

We are looking for a District Representative II located in on around the Lafayette, LA. This is your opportunity to join a global technology company, driving energy innovation for a balanced planet.

  •  Access to best-in-class resources, tools, technology and continuous education

  • Pride in working for a company that provides clean water, safe food, abundant energy and healthy environments

What You Will Do:

  • Work closely with current and new customers to understand business needs and recommend continuous improvement and innovation plans that will maintain and grow sales within assigned territory
  • Develop strong relationships with key stakeholders in current and new customers, including plant or facility executives. Leverage external network to pursue business opportunities within assigned territory
  • Generate and execute sales plans in assigned customer base and new customer accounts to meet defined territory profit increase goals
  • Engage in problem solving by performing system analysis, interpreting data and providing written recommendations to ensure customer operations are performing at optimal levels
  • Actively sell and support ChampionX innovations and technology in assigned customers to promote long-term business relationships with ChampionX
  • Begin to develop awareness of account profitability and overall health of account
  • Plan and lead customer trainings, events, seminars
  • Exhibit technical proficiency in a specified job area according to business group 

 

Pre-Employment Requirements:

  • Must have a valid Driver’s License
  • Acceptable Motor Vehicle Record

 

Position Details:

  • This is a 14/14 offshore chemical technician position
  • Ability to travel within assigned sales territory
  • Up to 50% overnight travel required to support sales territory

 

Minimum Qualifications:

  • High School or GED and a minimum of 5 years of relevant experience OR Bachelor's Degree and a minimum of 2 years of relevant experience
  • Immigration sponsorship not offered for this role
  • Experience in oilfield production and chemicals, oilfield chemicals, chemical treating, account management, or technical sales. 
  • Experience in technical sales, field sales support or account management experience

 

Physical Demands:

  • Role is deemed safety-sensitive and may be subject to employer or customer drug testing.
  • This role may involve management of or handling hazardous and non-hazardous wastes. As such, appropriate waste and waste minimization training will be required and tracked.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Chemical, Mechanical, Industrial), or Life Sciences (Biology, Chemistry, etc.)

job.title: Procurement & Logistics Apprentice
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration


RMSpumptools is seeking a driven Procurement & Logistics Apprentice located in Dyce, UK. The Procurement & Logistics Apprentice will be responsible for maintaining and updating information within our MRP system (EFACS) including updating supplier purchase order due dates, recording shipping information, and ensuring system data remains accurate and up to date.


If you have an interest in systems and learning about procurement then, we invite you to apply.


What’s in it For You:

The ability to make an impact and shape your career with a company that is passionate about growth


The support of an organisation that believes it is vital to include and engage diverse people, perspectives, and ideas to achieve our best


Thrive in a company that values sustainability, drives a safety-focused culture and empowers its employees through continuous improvement

Comprehensive benefits package & flexible working arrangements that enable balancing work commitments with other priorities


What You Will Do:


  • Maintain EFACS with supplier purchase order due dates and record shipping information
  • Data management ensuring system data is accurate and up to date
  • Reviewing written correspondence and extracting key information such as delivery dates and shipment updates
  • Assisting the Procurement Manager with tasks such as raising PO’s
  • Maintain a clean and safe work area as per company Health and Safety guidelines.
  • Identify and report any hazards or safety issues.
  • Always Work in a safe manner.
  • Ensure waste is recycled wherever possible
  • Ensure that you and others around your work area perform your duties in a safe and controlled manner
  • Follow all QHSE procedures relevant to your scope of work.

Preferred Skills:

job.title: Site Administrative Assistant
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.


We are looking for a Site Administrative Assistant for our Freeport, Texas location to provide comprehensive administrative, procurement, facilities, training, environmental, and employee support for our manufacturing site. This is your opportunity to join a global technology company driving energy innovation for a balanced planet.


This role serves as a key point of coordination for office operations, vendor management, compliance documentation, employee services, site communications, and business continuity activities. The position partners closely with site leadership, operations, HSE, finance, HR, and engineering teams to ensure efficient day-to-day site support and operational excellence.

 

What's In It For You


  • Opportunity to join a global technology company driving energy innovation for a balanced planet.
  • Opportunity for career growth and continuous development.
  • Thrive in a company that values safety, innovation, and operational excellence.
  • Comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company matching, and more!

 

What You Will Do

 

Office & Facilities Administration


  • Manage office supply inventory, including ordering, stocking, and maintaining supply cabinets throughout the site.
  • Coordinate management of site multifunction printers/copiers, including ordering consumables, arranging service and repairs, and processing related invoices.
  • Procure and maintain janitorial supplies not covered through established keepstock programs.
  • Provide general oversight of onsite janitorial services, ensuring facility support requirements are met and identifying service gaps for resolution.
  • Maintain a professional, organized, and functional administrative and engineering office environment.
  • Serve as a resource for office-related issues and facility support needs.

 

Employee Administration & Site Access


  • Create and manage employee badges and site access documentation until full integration into enterprise access systems.
  • Maintain and update site personnel lists, including employee additions, transfers, and terminations.
  • Coordinate issuance and tracking of employee safety footwear vouchers.
  • Coordinate issuance and tracking of prescription safety eyewear vouchers.
  • Create and maintain hurricane re-entry authorization letters and manage employee updates for emergency response plans.

 

Procurement & Financial Administration


  • Create purchase orders and process invoices through company procurement systems.
  • Establish and maintain vendor records and supporting documentation.
  • Execute approved purchases through contracted supplier catalogs and procurement channels.
  • Reconcile and submit monthly corporate card expense reports.
  • Prepare and submit monthly accrual information to site finance leadership.
  • Process vendor invoices and ensure accurate financial documentation and approvals.
  • Support budget tracking and procurement compliance activities.

 

Training & Compliance Support


  • Maintain employee profiles and training records within company training management systems.
  • Coordinate employee training schedules and communicate training requirements.
  • Maintain certifications, training completion records, and supporting documentation.
  • Support compliance reporting and administrative recordkeeping requirements.
  • Maintain employee training files in accordance with company and regulatory requirements.

 

Environmental, Health & Safety Support


  • Maintain site waste management records and ensure timely entry of disposal and manifest information.
  • Compile and generate the site's Annual Waste Summary report.
  • Maintain monthly permit tracking records and file required documentation.
  • Coordinate annual scale calibration certifications with appropriate technical resources.
  • Support environmental, health, safety, and regulatory documentation and recordkeeping requirements.

 

Employee Engagement & Site Events

  • Coordinate meal services for training sessions, meetings, site events, and employee celebrations.
  • Assist with planning and logistics for annual site events, including employee picnics and recognition programs.
  • Coordinate monthly employee birthday recognition activities.
  • Support employee engagement initiatives and special site functions.
  • Assist leadership teams with employee appreciation and culture-building activities.

 

Communications & Community Relations


  • Coordinate placement of approved site advertising and public notices.
  • Process charitable contribution and donation requests for leadership and finance approval.
  • Assist with preparation and distribution of site-wide communications and administrative updates.
  • Support community outreach activities and related administrative requirements.

 

Mail & Logistics Coordination


  • Manage outgoing and incoming mail and shipping activities.
  • Coordinate regular postal and courier service activities.
  • Support special mailing, shipping, and logistics requests as required.

 

Emergency Preparedness & Business Continuity


  • Manage seasonal activation and deactivation of emergency communication systems, including satellite communication services.
  • Maintain records supporting emergency preparedness and business continuity requirements.
  • Support site emergency response and hurricane readiness initiatives.

 

Customer Service & Administrative Support


  • Serve as a primary point of contact for visitors and guests, providing a professional and welcoming experience.
  • Assist employees, contractors, vendors, and managers with administrative requests and site-related support.
  • Support site managers and department leaders with special projects and administrative activities.
  • Maintain confidentiality when handling sensitive employee or business information.
  • Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

 

Pre-Employment Requirements


  • Must pass all pre-employment requirements as applicable.

 

Position Details


  • Work is performed in a manufacturing site environment.
  • Position provides administrative and operational support across multiple site functions, including operations, HSE, finance, HR, engineering, and site leadership.
  • Responsibilities may require movement throughout office, manufacturing, warehouse, and outdoor plant environments.
  • Local travel may be required for postal, shipping, vendor, or business-related activities.

 

Minimum Qualifications

 

Education


  • High school diploma or GED required.

 

Experience


  • Minimum of 3 years of administrative, office management, procurement, facilities coordination, or operations support experience.
  • Experience with purchasing, invoice processing, vendor management, and expense reporting.
  • Experience maintaining records, databases, and compliance documentation.

 

Technical Skills


  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite, including Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Teams.
  • Experience using enterprise procurement, accounting, or ERP systems such as GEP, SAP, Oracle, or equivalent platforms.
  • Experience with electronic recordkeeping and training management systems.
  • Ability to generate reports, maintain databases, and perform accurate data entry.

 

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities


  • Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple competing priorities.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong customer service and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work independently while maintaining strong collaboration with cross-functional teams.
  • Demonstrated attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Ability to maintain confidential and sensitive information.
  • Strong problem-solving, planning, and decision-making skills.
  • Ability to coordinate multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously.

 

Preferred Qualifications


  • Associate degree in Business Administration, Office Management, Accounting, Human Resources, or a related discipline.
  • Experience supporting multiple functions within a manufacturing, industrial, chemical, energy, or oilfield services environment.
  • Experience coordinating employee training, meetings, events, or similar administrative programs.
  • Experience supporting manufacturing, chemical processing, energy, or oilfield services operations.
  • Experience with environmental reporting, regulatory compliance documentation, training coordination, or safety program administration.
  • Working knowledge of environmental, health, safety, or regulatory recordkeeping processes.
  • Knowledge of procurement, budget tracking, purchase order management, and invoice processing.
  • Experience coordinating employee recognition programs, site communications, and employee engagement activities.

 

SLB Leadership & Behavioral Competencies


  • Demonstrates SLB values of People, Technology, and Performance.
  • Builds collaborative relationships across functions and organizational levels.
  • Promotes a positive employee experience through responsive service and professionalism.
  • Demonstrates initiative and a continuous improvement mindset.
  • Supports site operational excellence through effective planning, organization, and execution.
  • Maintains the highest standards of integrity, safety, and compliance.

 

Physical Requirements


  • Ability to move throughout office, manufacturing, warehouse, and outdoor plant environments.
  • Ability to occasionally lift and carry items weighing up to 25 pounds.
  • Ability to perform routine filing, stocking, inventory, and administrative support activities.
  • Ability to travel locally for postal, shipping, vendor, or business-related activities as required.

job.title: Regulatory Specialist I
job.description:

integration.


We are looking for a Regulatory Specialist - Middle East Regulatory Support to support our Middle East business within the Global Regulatory Affairs organization. This role will be located in Dubai, UAE. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced regulatory professional to work closely with commercial, product stewardship, and technical teams, ensuring compliance with regional chemical regulations while supporting business growth across the Middle East.


What's in it for You

  • The ability to make an impact and shape your career with a company that is dedicated to improving lives and passionate about growth.
  • The support of an organization that believes it is vital to include and engage diverse people, perspectives, and ideas to achieve our best
  • Thrive in a company that values sustainability, drives a safety-focused culture and empowers through continuous improvement
  • Develop expertise in regional and global chemical regulatory requirements and hazard communication.
  • Partner with a diverse, international team supporting customers and operations throughout the Middle East and Europe.
  • Opportunities for professional development and increased responsibility within a growing regulatory function.

What You Will Do

  • Provide regulatory support for ChampionX products and operations throughout the Middle East region and Europe.
  • Monitor and interpret regional chemical regulations and communicate compliance requirements to internal stakeholders.
  • Support product registrations, notifications, exemptions, and regulatory submissions as required by local authorities.
  • Prepare and maintain regulatory documentation, including Safety Data Sheets (SDSs), product classifications, labels, and compliance declarations.
  • Respond to customer requests regarding product regulatory status, chemical inventories, and compliance requirements.
  • Partner with Supply Chain, Technical Services, R&D, and Commercial teams to support business objectives while ensuring regulatory compliance.
  • Evaluate the regulatory impact of product, raw material, and formulation changes.
  • Support hazard communication activities in accordance with the Globally Harmonized System (GHS) and local regulatory requirements.
  • Assist with maintaining regulatory information within SAP and other business systems, ensuring data accuracy and consistency.
  • Participate in regulatory projects and continuous improvement initiatives related to data quality, compliance processes, and customer support.
  • Stay current on emerging regulatory developments and assess their potential impact on ChampionX products and business activities.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Environmental Science, Biological Sciences, or a related scientific discipline.
  • 5 years of experience in Regulatory Affairs, Product Stewardship, Chemical Compliance, or Hazard Communication within the chemical industry.
  • Working knowledge of global chemical regulations and hazard communication requirements.
  • Experience supporting product registrations, compliance reviews, or regulatory documentation.
  • Strong project management, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to interpret technical and regulatory documents and translate requirements into practical business guidance.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting regulatory compliance within the Middle East region.
  • Knowledge of chemical management regulations, GHS implementation, and regional product registration requirements.
  • Experience with SAP or regulatory data management systems.
  • Familiarity with global regulatory frameworks such as REACH, TSCA, AICIS, UK REACH, and other chemical inventory schemes.
  • Experience working in a multinational environment supporting multiple countries and stakeholders.

  • Employee is required to wear appropriate personal protective equipment including but not limited to shoes/boots, hard hats, or respirators.
  • Work is primarily executed on the production floor, with varying temperatures and high levels of noise; personal safety equipment such as glasses and protective shoes may be required.
  • Exposure to shop elements, such as, dust, petroleum-based products, and other chemicals.
  • Work may require visits to customer field locations in a variety of weather and temperature conditions.
  • May include working nights, weekends, and/or extended hours as the business need arises.

job.title: Reliability Engineering Co-Op
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.


We are looking for a motivated and enthusiastic undergraduate student to join our Reliability Engineering Co-Op Program in Sugar Land, Texas. This is your opportunity to join a global technology company, driving energy innovation for a balanced planet.


As a Reliability Engineering Co-Op, you will gain valuable hands-on experience supporting equipment reliability, preventive maintenance, asset performance, and continuous improvement initiatives within our Chemical Technologies division.

This opportunity combines engineering analysis with practical exposure to chemical manufacturing operations. You will collaborate with experienced reliability and process engineers, participate in equipment failure investigations, analyze maintenance data, and contribute to projects focused on improving equipment uptime and operational efficiency.

If you are eager to apply your classroom knowledge to real-world engineering challenges, develop your technical skills, and gain meaningful experience in an industrial manufacturing environment, we invite you to apply.


What's in It for You:


  • Hands-On Engineering Experience: Apply classroom knowledge to real-world reliability engineering, equipment performance, and chemical manufacturing challenges.
  • Professional Development: Gain practical exposure to reliability engineering methodologies, preventive maintenance strategies, Root Cause Analysis (RCA), and Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA).
  • Meaningful Projects: Contribute to reliability improvement initiatives designed to reduce equipment failures, improve asset performance, and support manufacturing uptime.
  • Collaboration and Mentorship: Work alongside experienced reliability and process engineers who will provide guidance, technical support, and professional development throughout the assignment.
  • Manufacturing Exposure: Gain firsthand experience in a chemical manufacturing plant, including equipment inspections, maintenance activities, and operational reliability assessments.
  • Career Development: Strengthen analytical, technical, problem-solving, communication, and project management skills while exploring potential career paths in reliability and manufacturing engineering.
  • Benefits: This position is benefits-eligible in accordance with applicable company policies and program guidelines.

What You Will Do:


Responsibilities may include:


  • Develop, maintain, and analyze equipment failure logs to identify recurring issues, equipment performance trends, and opportunities for reliability improvements.
  • Support Root Cause Analysis (RCA) investigations, including cause mapping, 5-Why analysis, and other structured problem-solving methodologies.
  • Assist with Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA) to evaluate potential equipment failures, assess operational risks, and identify preventive actions.
  • Support preventive maintenance (PM) program reviews and audits to evaluate maintenance effectiveness, documentation, and compliance with established procedures.
  • Assist with digitizing routine maintenance checklists and improving preventive maintenance documentation and tracking processes.
  • Review and align equipment Bills of Material (BOMs) with asset criticality assessments to support maintenance planning and equipment reliability.
  • Analyze equipment performance and maintenance data using Microsoft Excel and other available tools to identify trends and improvement opportunities.
  • Participate in supervised plant observations, equipment inspections, maintenance audits, and reliability assessments within a chemical manufacturing environment.
  • Collaborate with reliability engineers, process engineers, maintenance personnel, and operations teams to support equipment uptime and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Assist in developing technical documentation, reliability reports, maintenance recommendations, and project summaries.
  • Participate in team meetings, engineering discussions, and project reviews to gain exposure to manufacturing operations and engineering best practices.
  • Prepare a final presentation summarizing assigned projects, key findings, accomplishments, lessons learned, and recommendations for future improvements.
  • Complete all required plant safety training and demonstrate a commitment to site safety procedures, personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements, and safe work practices.

Minimum Qualifications:


  • Currently pursuing a bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Reliability Engineering, or a closely related engineering discipline from an accredited college or university.
  • Must be authorized to work in the United States without current or future employer immigration sponsorship.
  • Ability and willingness to work in a chemical manufacturing environment and comply with all applicable safety requirements.

Preferred Qualifications:


  • Currently enrolled as a sophomore or junior in an undergraduate engineering program.
  • Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0.
  • Strong interest in reliability engineering, equipment maintenance, manufacturing operations, or asset performance improvement.
  • Basic understanding of mechanical systems, engineering principles, and industrial equipment.
  • Familiarity with reliability engineering concepts, preventive maintenance practices, or equipment failure analysis.
  • Exposure to Root Cause Analysis (RCA), 5-Why methodologies, or Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA).
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret data, identify trends, and communicate findings.
  • Previous internship, Co-Op, academic project, manufacturing, maintenance, or other relevant technical experience.
  • Familiarity with Computerized Maintenance Management Systems (CMMS) or Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) systems is beneficial but not required.
  • Previous military technical experience or skilled trades experience, particularly for students returning to pursue an engineering degree.
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, organizational, and teamwork skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively with cross-functional engineering, maintenance, and operations teams.
  • Demonstrated initiative, attention to detail, adaptability, and willingness to learn in a hands-on industrial environment.

Additional Information:


This Reliability Engineering Co-Op opportunity is based in Sugar Land, Texas, and provides exposure to both engineering activities and chemical manufacturing operations.

The student will support reliability-driven projects focused on improving equipment uptime, strengthening preventive maintenance practices, and enhancing the performance of critical manufacturing assets.

The assignment will include opportunities to work alongside experienced engineering professionals, observe plant operations, participate in supervised field activities, and contribute to meaningful reliability improvement projects.

A designated reliability engineering mentor and process engineering buddy will provide guidance, technical support, and professional development throughout the assignment.

The program is designed to provide valuable real-world engineering experience, help students strengthen their professional resumes, and support their exploration of future full-time career opportunities in reliability engineering, manufacturing, and related technical disciplines.

job.description:

What You Will Do:

  • Install, maintain, troubleshoot, and repair mechanical systems and equipment and facility systems such as electrical and building systems.
  • Interpret blueprints and schematics.
  • Develop and perform preventative maintenance
  • General facility support which may include the occasional use of company truck
  • Execution of capital projects

Pre-Employment requirements:

  • Drug screen
  • Background Check

 

Minimum Qualifications:  

  • Prior maintenance experience
  • Metal fabrication and welding experience
  • Working knowledge of hand & power tools, overhead crane
  • Basic computer skills, including Microsoft Office Suite
  • Understanding of industrial electrical, including single phase and 3 phase power
  • Ability to read and interpret machine drawings and electrical schematics
  • Advanced organization and time management skills
  • Able to troubleshoot equipment
  • Able to repair equipment
  • Understanding of testing equipment and criteria
  • Motivated and self-starter for solving issues and problems
  • Knowledge of methods, practices and techniques of maintaining building and facilities
  • Read, write, and speak English fluently
  • Willing to work overtime and Saturdays as required
  • Immigration sponsorship not offered for this role

 

Physical Demands:

  • Role is deemed safety-sensitive and may be subject to employer or customer drug testing.
  • The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.  Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

 

Physical Activities

  • Medium work:  Exerting up to 50 pounds of force occasionally and/or up to 20 pounds of force frequently, and/or up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects.
  • Ascending or descending ladders, stairs, scaffolding, ramps, poles and the like, using feet and legs and/or hands and arms. Body agility is emphasized.
  • Maintaining body equilibrium to prevent falling when walking, standing, or crouching on narrow, slippery, or erratically moving surfaces.
  • Bending body downward and forward by bending spine at the waist. This factor is important if it occurs to a considerable degree and requires full use of the lower extremities and back muscles.
  • Bending legs at knee to come to a rest on knees.
  • Bending the body downward and forward by bending leg and spine.
  • Moving about on hands and knees or hands and feet.
  • Extending hand(s) and arm(s) in any direction.
  • Moving about on foot to accomplish tasks, particularly for long distances or moving from one work site to another.
  • Using upper extremities to press against something with steady force in order to thrust forward, downward, or outward.
  • Using upper extremities to exert force in order to draw, drag, haul, or tug objects in a sustained motion.
  • Raising objects from a lower to a higher position or moving objects horizontally from position to position.
  • Picking, pinching, typing, or otherwise working, primarily with fingers rather than the whole hand or arm as in handling.
  • Applying pressure to an object with the fingers and palm.
  • Perceiving attributes of objects, such as size, shape, temperature, or texture by touching with skin, particularly that of fingertips.
  • Expressing or exchanging ideas by means of the spoken word.  Those activities in which they must convey detailed or important spoken instructions to customer or other workers accurately, loudly, or quickly.
  • Perceiving the nature of sounds at normal speaking levels with or without correction.  Ability to receive detailed information through oral communication, and to make the discriminations in sound.
  • Substantial movement (motions) of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers to use a computer.

 

Work Environment:

  • Indoor and outdoor environmental conditions. Activities occur indoors and outdoors
  • Extreme heat. Temperatures above 100 degrees for periods of more than one hour. Consideration should be given to the effect of other environmental conditions, such as wind and humidity
  • Hazards includes a variety of physical conditions, such as proximity to moving mechanical parts, moving vehicles, electrical current, or exposure to chemicals
  • Atmospheric conditions that affect the respiratory system or skin may include fumes, odors, dust, mists, gases, or poor ventilation
  • Potential skin exposure to oils and other cutting fluids

 

Visual Acuity

  • The employee is required to have close visual acuity to perform an activity such as: visual inspection involving small defects, small parts and/or operation of machines (including inspection), using measurement devices, and/or assembly or fabrication of parts at distances close to the eyes.
  • The employee is required to have visual acuity to operate motor vehicles.
  • The employee is required to have visual acuity to determine the accuracy, neatness, thoroughness of work assigned or to make general observations of facilities or structures.

What’s In It For You:

  • The support of an organization that believes it is vital to include and engage diverse people, perspectives, and ideas to achieve our best·

job.title: Procurement Analyst - Global Operations
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

 

We are looking for a Procurement Analyst – Global Operations located in Sugar Land, Texas. This role is expected to partner closely with our global and regional procurement teams, global finance shared service center, department buyers for source to pay activities including but not limited to: vendor onboarding, material pricing, purchase requisition to purchase order conversion, manage invoice disputes, and serves as a subject matter expert in either processes, systems or compliance.

 

This role will also be actively engaged in the testing and execution of the future Source to Pay process environment, collaborate with suppliers to create punch out or hosted catalogs, convert PR to PO for materials and services not covered by catalogs, train end users on the current and future procurement processes

 

What’s in it for You


  • Access to best-in-class tools, technology, and continuous learning opportunities
  • A strong safety culture with industry-leading training and personal protective equipment
  • Professional growth and career development opportunities within ChampionX and SLB
  • Comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, and 401(k) with company match

 

What You Will Do


Source to Pay Process Assessment & Standardization


  • Lead the mapping and documentation of end-to-end Source-to-Pay processes across both PCT legacy organizations, including sourcing, contracting, purchasing, invoicing, and payment activities to bring MPC legacy into the PCT Direct Procurement Model and prepape future S4 integration.
  • Develop actionable recommendations and roadmaps to drive process efficiency, automation, simplification, and standardization.
  • Support change management and implementation activities required to transition to common ways of working.

Procurement Operations Support


  • Provide Subject Matter expertise in procurement operations and actively support day-to-day procurement activities by executing, optimizing and serving as a key resource across all core procurement operational processes.
  • Maintain procurement master data and ensure compliance with established processes and policies.
  • Support Procurement reporting and operational performance reviews

Sustainability & Scope 3 Emissions


  • Support Scope 3 emissions tracking and reporting by collaborating with suppliers to collect sustainability and emissions data.
  • Monitor data collection progress, validate data quality, and assist in identifying opportunities to improve supply chain sustainability performance.

Key Responsibilities


  • Strong expertise in Source to Pay process mapping, analysis and standardization.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify, quantity, and implement process efficiency improvements and standardization initiatives.
  • Experience leading cross functional workshops and collaborating with stakeholders across global organizations.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to leverage data and metrics to drive decision-making and continuous improvement
  • Excellent problem solving capabilities with experience evaluating systems, workflows and process controls.
  • Ability to influence stakeholders and drive alignment across multiple legacy organizations and business functions,
  • Excellent communication, facilitation and documentation skills.
  • Strong SAP Procurement experience in a procurement, shared services or process excellence environment
  • Experience with a source to pay platform like GEP or SAP Ariba is preferred.
  • Demonstrates integrity, accountability and a continuous improvement mindset

Minimum Qualifications


  • Bachelor’s degree in business, Supply Chain, Finance, Engineering or a related field is preferred.
  • 5 years professional experience in procurement, shared services, Process excellence or business transformation role.
  • Proven experience mapping and redesigning processes
  • Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from suppliers and internal customers.
  • Ability to work in a deadline-driven work environment, attention to details and ability to multi-task.

 

About Us

Our teams are committed to developing innovative technologies that support a future with more energy and less carbon.

job.description:

  • personal protection equipment

What You Will Do:

  • Lead and execute routine and non-routine analytical testing activities in support of customer programs, field operations, and laboratory service commitments.
  • Apply advanced production chemistry knowledge and sound technical judgment to troubleshoot challenges, validate methods, interpret analytical data, and solve complex problems.
  • Support customer programs by designing, conducting, and interpreting laboratory analyses tied to real-world field performance and operational outcomes.
  • Independently manage multiple priorities, project deadlines, customer requests, and stakeholder communications in a fast-paced laboratory environment.
  • Manage high volumes of routine analytical testing while maintaining quality, accuracy, data integrity, and turnaround time expectations.
  • Operate, maintain, troubleshoot, and optimize laboratory instrumentation while ensuring compliance with established QA/QC procedures and laboratory standards.
  • Support the mentoring, training, and development of chemists, technicians, and technologists through coaching, knowledge sharing, and technical guidance.
  • Collaborate with field personnel, sales, technical teams, and customers to translate analytical data into actionable recommendations.
  • Identify opportunities for process improvements that enhance laboratory efficiency, quality, safety, and customer service.
  • Champion safety culture, support continuous improvement initiatives, and contribute positively to overall laboratory performance, efficiency, and team effectiveness.
  • Perform miscellaneous administrative tasks.

 

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Chemistry or related field with at least 2 years of US Land oilfield production chemistry experience, or
  • Master's degree in Chemistry or related field with at least 1 years of US Land oilfield production chemistry experience
  • Demonstrated experience supporting production chemistry programs for U.S. land-based oil and gas operations.
  • Experience managing high volumes of routine analytical testing while maintaining quality, accuracy, and turnaround time expectations.
  • Proven ability to follow SOPs, work independently, prioritize competing demands, and manage moderately complex projects with minimal supervision.
  • Experience operating and troubleshooting ICP-OES, Ion Chromatography (IC), Gas Chromatography (GC), XRF, or equivalent analytical instrumentation.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, etc) and Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS), with experience leveraging data management and reporting tools to support laboratory operations, decision-making, and process improvement. 

 

Physical Demands:

  • Must have the ability to Lift/Push/Pull/Carry up to 55 pounds chest high
  • Role is deemed safety-sensitive and may be subject to employer or customer drug testing

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 3-7 years of experience in oilfield production chemistry, chemical manufacturing, or industrial analytical laboratory environments.
  •  3+ years of laboratory leadership, technical leadership, mentoring, or senior laboratory experience supporting production chemistry operations.
  • Demonstrated history of taking ownership of laboratory responsibilities, following through on commitments, and consistently delivering high-quality results.
  • Proven ability to foster a collaborative, respectful, and solutions-oriented work environment through effective communication and constructive engagement with colleagues and stakeholders.
  • Experience presenting technical findings, managing projects, and collaborating effectively across functional teams.
  • Understanding of customer needs and ability to translate analytical data into actionable operational insights.
  • Experience identifying and implementing process improvements that enhance laboratory efficiency, quality, safety, or customer service.
  • Experience with Six Sigma, Lean, or continuous improvement methodologies in a manufacturing or factory setting.

We have an immediate need for an Operational Specialist in Vernal, Utah.  If you are a dedicated DOT driving professional with a proven track record of success in customer delivery, we invite you to apply.  This is your opportunity to join a large growing company offering a competitive base hourly rate and benefits.

  • You will join a growing company offering competitive pay and benefits
  • Access to best in class resources, tools, and technology

  • Knowledge of precautions needed if exposed to H2S (hydrogen sulfide)

  • Experience performing warehouse duties, which include preventative maintenance, inventory and ordering of chemicals, receiving incoming shipments, organizing warehouse for safe and efficient chemical storage, operation of customized chemical manufacturing equipment and the upkeep of warehouse grounds
